chunks: And from him, from several of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ali ibn Bilal, from al-Hasan ibn Bassam al-Jammal, from a man who said:

I was with Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) between Mecca and Medina. He was fasting in the month of Sha'ban. Then we saw the crescent of the month of Ramadan, so he broke his fast. I said to him, 'May I be your ransom, yesterday was from Sha'ban and he was fasting, and today is from the month of Ramadan and he is breaking his fast.' He said, 'That was voluntary (fasting), and we may do what we wish, but this is obligatory (fasting), so we may do only what we are commanded.'

key_terms.أَفْطَرَ: Broke his fast (ended the daily fast)
key_terms.تَطَوُّعٌ: Voluntary (referring to non-obligatory acts of worship)
key_terms.رَمَضَانَ: Ramadan (the ninth month of the Islamic lunar calendar, month of obligatory fasting)
key_terms.شَعْبَانَ: Sha'ban (the eighth month of the Islamic lunar calendar)
key_terms.صَائِمٌ: Fasting (abstaining from food, drink, etc. from dawn to sunset)
key_terms.فَرْضٌ: Obligatory (referring to mandatory acts of worship)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on breaking fast upon sighting the Ramadan crescent if one was fasting voluntarily in Sha'ban?
ai.summary: This narration from Sahih al-Tusi highlights the jurisprudential distinction between voluntary (Tatawwu') and obligatory (Fard) fasting, illustrating the Imam's flexibility in voluntary acts versus his strict adherence to command in obligatory ones. It underscores the Shia principle that voluntary worship allows for personal discretion, while obligatory duties require precise compliance with divine instruction, a concept rooted in the flexibility granted to travelers and the sick. The incident occurred in Sha'ban, emphasizing the transition from the month of preparation to the month of obligation.
